components.name: Avatar
components.purpose: A person or thing as a small round picture, falling back to initials, then to an icon.
components.use: Beside a name in a list, a comment or a menu, and in an AvatarGroup for the people on something.
components.avoid: For a logo or a photo that is content, use an img; for a status on the avatar, wrap it in a Chip.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an avatar is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: src
props.description: The image's address.

props.name: alt
props.description: Who or what it shows ("Ada Lovelace"): the image's alt, and the source of the initials.

props.name: text
props.description: Text in place of the initials from alt, such as a short code.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon shown with neither image nor name; without it, a silhouette.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 24 px, `md` 32 px, `lg` 40 px. In an AvatarGroup, the group's size wins.

components.notes:
It shows `src` when it loads. With no `src`, or when the image fails (also
when it failed before an island hydrated), it shows initials: `text` if
given, else the first letters of the first and last words of `alt`
("Ada Lovelace" is AL). With neither, it shows `icon`, a Lucide name, or
without one a silhouette it draws itself (so no icon ships for it).

`alt` names it: the image's alt text, or, for initials and icon, the
avatar's `aria-label` with `role="img"`. Without `alt` it is decorative.
`size` is `sm` (24 px), `md` (32 px) or `lg` (40 px); in an AvatarGroup the
group's size wins.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.purpose: Avatars overlapping in a row, showing the first few and counting the rest.
components.use: For the people on a project, a thread or a document, where the faces matter more than the names.
components.avoid: For a list a person reads name by name, use a list with an Avatar beside each name.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the group is not a hit target.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; set max so the row fits the narrowest place it appears.

props.name: max
props.description: How many avatars to show; the rest are counted. Unset or 0 shows all.

props.name: size
props.description: The size of every avatar in the group.

components.notes:
Put Avatars in its default slot. With `max`, the first `max` show and a last
avatar counts the rest, drawn `+3` and read as "3 more"; without it every
avatar shows. `size` sizes
every avatar in the group.

It is a `group`: name it with an `aria-label` ("Project members"). Avatars
join the group in the order they render, on the server and in the browser
alike, so the count hydrates as rendered.

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: A short label for a status, a category or a count, drawn in a tone.
components.use: Beside a title or in a table cell, to say a state at a glance (Paid, Failed, Beta, 3).
components.avoid: For something a person can press or remove, use Button; for an indicator on the corner of an icon or avatar, use Chip.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; a badge is not a hit target.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a badge does not wrap.

props.name: label
props.description: The badge's text; the default slot replaces it.

props.name: variant
props.description: `solid` to stand out, `soft` and `outline` to sit quietly beside text, `ghost` for tone alone.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `success` for done, `danger` for failed.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label; alone, the badge is square.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the label.

components.notes:
`variant` is `solid`, `soft`, `outline` or `ghost`; `tone` is `neutral`,
`primary`, `danger`, `warning` or `success`; `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`.
Give the text as `label` or as the default slot. Icons are decorative, so the
text must carry the meaning; with only an icon the badge is square and needs
an `aria-label`.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: A button that runs an action, or a link drawn as a button when it has `to`.
components.use: For the actions on a page, a form's submit, a dialog's confirm; solid for the one main action, soft, outline or ghost for the others.
components.avoid: For moving to another page within running text, use Link; for a choice that stays on or off, use a switch or checkbox.

adapts.input: On touch an md button is at least 44 px tall (--weft-hit-min); a small or square button keeps its drawn size and grows its hit area to 44 px through a pseudo-element. Hover colours apply only where the device can hover.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; set block to fill a narrow column.

props.name: label
props.description: The button's text; the default slot replaces it.

props.name: variant
props.description: `solid` for the main action, `soft` and `outline` for secondary ones, `ghost` for the quietest.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `danger` for destructive actions.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`. On touch an md button grows to 44 px; sm keeps its height and grows its hit area.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the label; alone, the button is square and needs an `aria-label`. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the label. The trailing slot replaces it.

props.name: square
props.description: Square, its width equal to its height, whatever it holds.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress: shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and blocks activation, keeping width and focus.

props.name: loadingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon to turn in place of the spinner while loading.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: a button is natively disabled; a link loses its address.

props.name: active
props.description: Drawn as on: the current one of a set. With `to` it is the current page (aria-current="page").

props.name: block
props.description: Fill the width of the container.

props.name: to
props.description: An address: the button renders as an `<a>` that goes there (rel="noopener" when it is another site).

props.name: rel
props.description: With `to`: the native rel; `noopener` is added for another site.

props.name: target
props.description: With `to`: where to open it, as the native attribute: `_blank` for a new tab.

props.name: type
props.description: The native button type; `submit` submits its form. Ignored with `to`.

emits.name: click
emits.description: Pressed by mouse, touch or keyboard; never while loading or disabled.

components.notes:
`variant` is `solid`, `soft`, `outline` or `ghost`; `tone` is `neutral`,
`primary`, `danger`, `warning` or `success`; `size` is `sm`, `md` or `lg`.
Give the text as `label` or as the default slot; the `leading` and
`trailing` slots replace `icon` and `trailing-icon`. With only an icon the
button is square (`square` makes any button square): give it an
`aria-label`, or it warns once in development. `active` draws it as the
current one of a set; with `to` it also sets `aria-current="page"`.

**Touch:** an md button grows to 44 px tall on touch, so the visible target
is the hit target. A small or square button keeps its size (a toolbar would
change shape otherwise) and its `::before` reaches 44 px instead.

**Loading** shows a spinner (or `loading-icon`, turning) over the content,
which stays in place (hidden), so the button keeps its width. It sets `aria-busy="true"` and
`aria-disabled="true"`, and blocks activation by mouse, keyboard and form
submit, but stays focusable, so a keyboard user does not lose their place.

**Disabled** is the native `disabled` attribute on a button. With `to` the
button is an `<a>`, taking `rel` and `target`, with `noopener` added for
another site; disabled, it has no address and is announced as a disabled
link; loading, it keeps its address (and focus) but neither a click, a
middle click nor Enter follows it.

**Keyboard:** a native button, so Enter and Space press it; as a link, Enter
follows it. Focus shows the theme's focus ring.

**In a Form.** As a link it is disabled while the Form is disabled or busy,
so a Cancel cannot navigate mid-submit (a disabled fieldset disables native
buttons but leaves links alone). While the Form is busy, a `type="submit"`
button loads and any other button ignores presses, both keeping focus.

`click` is emitted only when the button is pressed while neither loading nor
disabled. `type` defaults to `button`, so a Button inside a form submits it
only with `type="submit"`.

components.purpose: A bordered surface holding related content, with an optional header, actions and footer.

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: A box to tick on its own or as one of a CheckboxGroup, which can also be indeterminate.
components.use: For a yes or no that is sent with a form (accept the terms), or a choice among several that are all allowed.
components.avoid: For a setting that takes effect at once, use Switch; for one choice among several, use RadioGroup.

adapts.input: The box keeps its drawn size; the native input lies over it at least --weft-hit-min square, and each row is at least --weft-hit-min tall, so on touch it takes a 44 px press without neighbours' hit areas overlapping.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a long label wraps beside the box.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: Ticked (`true`), not (`false`), or `'indeterminate'`; bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The state to start in when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the box. The default slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the label, which also describes the box.

props.name: value
props.description: The value it stands for: what a CheckboxGroup lists, and what a form post sends (default `on`).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a group's or a FormField's applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the ticked box.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Ticked or unticked by a press, Space or its label.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The native change.

components.notes:
Bind `v-model` to `true`, `false` or `'indeterminate'`. Indeterminate (some
of what it stands for is chosen) draws a dash and is announced as mixed; a
press ticks it. A parent that does not take a change leaves it as bound.

It is a native checkbox, so Space toggles it, its label toggles it, and it
posts `value` (default `on`) under `name` with a plain form. `label` (or the
default slot) is beside the box; `description` sits under the label and
describes the box. Focus rings the drawn box.

In a CheckboxGroup a Checkbox with a `value` is ticked while that value is in
the group's list. In a FormField it takes the field's id, so the field's label
also names it.

examples.source:
<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { computed, ref } from 'vue'
import { Checkbox, Stack } from '@weft/ui'

const files = ref([
  { name: 'report.pdf', on: true },
  { name: 'notes.txt', on: false },
])
const all = computed({
  get: () => (files.value.every((f) => f.on) ? true : files.value.some((f) => f.on) ? 'indeterminate' : false),
  set: (v: boolean | 'indeterminate') => files.value.forEach((f) => (f.on = v === true)),
})
</script>

    <Checkbox v-for="f in files" :key="f.name" v-model="f.on" :label="f.name" />

</template>

components.name: CheckboxGroup
components.purpose: Several checkboxes for one list of chosen values.
components.use: For choosing any number of a few options, all in view (toppings, notification channels).
components.avoid: For exactly one choice, use RadioGroup; for many options, use a multiple select.

adapts.input: Each row is at least 44 px tall on touch, and each box's hit area 44 px square, so rows do not steal each other's presses.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Horizontal groups wrap onto more rows when narrow.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen values, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The values chosen at first when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: items
props.description: The options: values, or `{ value, label, description, disabled }`.

props.name: legend
props.description: The group's name, shown above it; inside a FormField the field's label names it instead.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name each box posts under; a FormField's applies when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`, for every box.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the ticked boxes.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` (a column) or `horizontal` (a wrapping row).

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every box.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A box was ticked or unticked: the new list.

components.notes:
Bind the list with `v-model`. Give the options as `items` - values, or
`{ value, label, description, disabled }` - or put Checkboxes with a `value`
in the default slot. A ticked value is added at the end of the list.

It is a `<fieldset>`: `legend` names it, or, inside a FormField, the field's
label does through `aria-labelledby`; the field's description, hint and error describe the
group, and an error marks it `aria-invalid`. The boxes keep ids of their own.
`disabled` disables every box. Tab visits each box, as native checkboxes do.

components.name: Chip
components.purpose: A small indicator, a dot or a short count, on the corner of what it wraps.
components.use: For unread counts on an icon, online status on an avatar, a mark that something changed.
components.avoid: For a status in a line of text, use Badge.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the indicator is not a hit target, the wrapped content is.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: text
props.description: A short count or mark inside the indicator; without it the indicator is a dot.

props.name: label
props.description: What the indicator means, for assistive technology ("3 unread messages"); the drawn indicator is then hidden from it.

props.name: tone
props.description: The indicator's colour and what it says.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: position
props.description: Which corner: `top-end`, `bottom-end`, `top-start` or `bottom-start`.

props.name: inset
props.description: Sit inside the corner rather than across it, for round content such as an avatar.

props.name: show
props.description: Show the indicator; false hides it and keeps the content.

components.notes:
Wrap the content in the default slot. `text` puts a short count or mark in
the indicator; without it the indicator is a dot. `position` is logical
(`top-end`, `bottom-end`, `top-start`, `bottom-start`), so `top-end` is the
top right in a left-to-right document and the top left in a right-to-left
one. `inset` keeps the indicator inside the corner, for round content.
`show` hides it, keeping the content.

Give `label` ("3 unread messages") to say what the indicator means: it is
read to assistive technology and the drawn indicator is hidden from it.

components.name: ConfirmDialog
components.purpose: Asks the user to confirm an action before it goes ahead, with Cancel and a confirm button.
components.use: Before an action that is hard to undo: delete, discard changes, leave without saving.
components.avoid: For an action that can be undone, do it and offer Undo in a toast; for a form, use Dialog.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; its buttons follow Button's touch sizes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: As Dialog: full-screen when the viewport is narrow.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: title
props.description: The question, which names the dialog.

props.name: description
props.description: What happens if the action goes ahead.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: The confirm button's text: say the action (`Delete`).

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: The cancel button's text.

props.name: tone
props.description: The confirm button's colour: `danger` for an action that destroys.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description: Run on confirm; a promise it returns keeps the dialog open, loading, until it settles. Given by `@confirm`.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed.

emits.name: cancel
emits.description: Answered no: Cancel, Escape or the backdrop.

components.notes:
It has no stylesheet of its own: it is a Dialog with `role="alertdialog"`
(WAI-ARIA APG, Alert and Message Dialogs) and two Buttons.

`title` is the question, `description` what happens; `confirm-label` names
the action (`Delete`) and `tone="danger"` colours it for one that destroys.
Focus starts on Cancel, the safe answer.

`@confirm` runs on confirm and the dialog closes. When the handler returns a
promise, the confirm button loads and nothing closes the dialog until the
promise settles: it closes when the work succeeds and stays, ready again,
when it fails, so the person can retry or cancel. Cancel, Escape and the
backdrop emit `cancel` and close it. The default slot is the trigger, or bind
`v-model:open`; the `body` slot adds content under the description.

components.purpose: A menu for an area, opened in place of the browser's own by a right press, the context menu key or a long press.
components.use: For actions on an item that a power user expects on right press (a file, a row, a canvas), alongside a visible way to reach them.
components.avoid: As the only way to an action, since nothing shows that it is there; give the item a DropdownMenu button too.

the menu is a DropdownMenu, with the same keyboard, submenus and closing.

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: A modal window over the page, for a task or message that needs the user's attention before going back.
components.use: For a short form, a decision or details that interrupt the page on purpose: rename, invite, settings of one thing.
components.avoid: To confirm an action, use ConfirmDialog; for a panel at the edge (navigation, filters), Sheet; for a hint, Tooltip or Popover.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; on touch its close button's hit area is at least 44 px.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Centred, at most 32rem wide; when the viewport is narrow (under 640 px) it is full-screen, as it is at every width with `fullscreen`.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, which names the dialog. Without one, give the dialog an `aria-label`.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, which describes the dialog.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button (×) in the header.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press on the backdrop close it.

props.name: fullscreen
props.description: Full-screen at every width; it is full-screen when narrow anyway.

props.name: role
props.description: `alertdialog` for a dialog that needs an answer before going on (ConfirmDialog uses it).

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, the backdrop or a close.

components.notes:
The default slot is the trigger, one element (a Button), which opens it and
carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; or
bind `v-model:open`. `title` names it and `description` describes it
(`aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`). The `body` and `footer` slots get
`close()`; `header` replaces the title and description, and `actions` adds
controls before the close button (×, drawn inline; `close="false"` hides it).

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal) pattern: `aria-modal="true"`,
focus trapped inside, starting on the first tabbable element that is not the
close button, and the page does not scroll while it is open.

**Closing.** Escape, a press on the backdrop and the close button close it;
`dismissible="false"` keeps it open on Escape and the backdrop. Focus returns
to its trigger, after a press on the backdrop too (the backdrop is the
dialog's own), or, with no trigger, to the element that had focus when it
opened.

Its content renders into `#weft-overlays` only once mounted, so the server
renders none of it; attributes go to the dialog element.

props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

off by default (`close` shows it). Otherwise it is a Sheet, with the same

the backdrop, focus back on the trigger. `dismissible="false"` turns off
dragging as well.

drag.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.purpose: A menu of actions opened from a button, with groups, checkbox and radio items, links and submenus.
components.use: For the actions on one thing (a row's More button), a user menu, view options.
components.avoid: To choose a value for a form, use a select; for navigation between pages, links or navigation components.

adapts.input: On pointer it floats beside its trigger and a submenu opens beside its item, on hover too. On touch it is a bottom sheet with large items, 48 px tall with larger text, and a submenu is a sheet above it, with a back item. The input can change while it is open; the focused item stays focused.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Floating, it is at least 10rem wide and stays within the room left; as a sheet, the viewport's width.

props.name: items
props.description: The items, or groups of them (an array of arrays), drawn with separators between.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where it floats against the trigger on pointer (start and end follow the text direction).

props.name: anchor
props.type: { getBoundingClientRect(): DOMRect /** For a point: the element it belongs to, whose scrolling and direction the overlay follows. */ contextElement?: Element }
props.description: Float against this element or point instead of the trigger (ContextMenu gives the pointer's).

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed.

components.notes:
`items` is a list of `MenuItem`s, or a list of groups (an array of arrays),
drawn with separators between. An item has `label`, `icon` (a Lucide name),
`tone` (`danger`), `disabled`, `to` and `target` (a link), `children` (a
submenu) and `onSelect(event)`; `type: 'label'` is a group's heading,
`'separator'` a line, `'checkbox'` and `'radio'` items with `checked` and
`onUpdateChecked(checked)`. The `item` slot replaces an item's label.

It follows the WAI-ARIA APG Menu Button and Menu patterns. The trigger, the
default slot (one element), gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`
and `aria-controls`, and the menu is labelled by it.

**Keyboard.** On the trigger: Enter, Space and ArrowDown open the menu on
its first item, ArrowUp on its last. In the menu: ArrowDown and ArrowUp move
(looping), Home and End go to the ends, typing jumps to the item whose label
starts so, Enter and Space choose. ArrowRight opens a submenu on its first
item, ArrowLeft closes it back to its item (mirrored right to left). Escape
closes one level; Tab closes the menu. Disabled items are reached but cannot
be chosen.

**Choosing** an item calls `onSelect`, closes every level and puts focus back
on the trigger, unless `onSelect` calls `event.preventDefault()`. A checkbox
item calls `onUpdateChecked(!checked)`, a radio item `onUpdateChecked(true)`.
A press outside closes it; while it is open the page does not scroll.

The menu renders into `#weft-overlays` once mounted; attributes go to it.
`anchor` positions it against another element or a point (ContextMenu).

components.purpose: Controls joined into one, their borders meeting.
components.use: For an input with a button at its end, a unit before an amount, a row of segmented buttons.
components.avoid: For laying out separate fields, use Stack or Grid.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the controls in it keep their touch sizes, so on touch an md input and an md Button in a group are both 44 px tall.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a vertical group stacks its controls.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (a row) or `vertical` (a column).

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`, for the form controls in it.

components.notes:
Put Inputs, InputNumbers and Buttons in the default slot. Neighbouring borders
overlap, only the group's outer corners are round, and the focused control is
drawn on top so its ring shows whole. `orientation` is `horizontal` or
`vertical`. Form controls in it take its `size` unless they set their own;
give Buttons in it the same `size`. It is a `role="group"`; give it an
`aria-label` when the controls need a shared name.

components.name: Form
components.purpose: A form that checks its values against a Weft field schema before it submits.
components.use: For any form whose values need checking before they are sent, with the same rules the server enforces.
components.avoid: For a search box or a single setting that takes effect at once, a Form is not needed.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the fields inside it adapt.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; its fields stack in a column.

props.name: state
props.description: The values, by field name: an object the fields bind into with `v-model`.

props.name: schema
props.description: The rules each field must meet, by name: `{ email: { required: true, email: true } }`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every control in it, buttons too, and a submit does nothing.

props.name: loading
props.description: Busy: as disabled, and `aria-busy`, so a second submit does nothing.

props.name: loadingAuto
props.description: Busy on its own while the submit handler's promise is pending.

props.name: onSubmit
props.description: Bound with `@submit`: runs once every field is valid, with a copy of the values; a promise it returns keeps the form busy.

emits.name: error
emits.description: Submitted with errors: each failing field's sentence, by name.

components.notes:
`state` is the values, an object the fields bind into with `v-model`;
`schema` is a Weft field schema - plain JSON a server can send, the same
shape the Go contract will generate - keyed by field name:

    { email: { required: true, email: true }, age: { min: 18, message: 'You must be 18 or over.' } }

Each rule is optional: `required`, `min` and `max` (a length for text and
lists, bounds for numbers), `pattern` (matched against the whole text, as the
HTML attribute does), `email`, and `message` in place of the default
sentences. Its TypeScript type is `FieldSchema`, and `validateFields` checks
values against one anywhere.

**When it checks.** On submit every field is checked. With errors, `error`
fires with them, each FormField with a matching `name` shows its error, and
focus moves to the first invalid control; without, the `@submit` handler
runs with a deep copy of the values (lists and objects too), typed as
`state` is. After the first submit, a field is checked again when it is
left, and a field showing an error is checked as it changes, so the error
goes the moment it is fixed - but no new error appears while typing.

**Server errors.** A template ref's `setErrors({ email: 'That address is
taken.' })` shows errors from elsewhere. Leaving such a field keeps its error
(the server said so, and nothing changed); changing the field checks it
again. `validate()` checks without submitting, and `clear()` clears every
error.

A server error on a field the schema has no rule for clears the first time
that field changes: there is nothing to check it against.

**Disabled.** The content sits in a `<fieldset>` with no frame, so
`disabled` disables every control in the form at once - Weft's and native
ones, Buttons included - and a submit does nothing. A fieldset leaves links
alone, so a Link, or a Button with `to`, in the form reads it and is
disabled as a disabled link is: no address, `aria-disabled`, no navigation.

**Busy.** `loading`, or with `loading-auto` (on by default) a `@submit`
handler that returns a promise, makes the form busy until it settles: it sets
`aria-busy`, a second press or Enter submits nothing, its fields are
disabled and its links have no address. Its buttons are not natively
disabled, so the submit button keeps focus: it shows its spinner and is
`aria-busy` and `aria-disabled`, and any other button is `aria-disabled`,
all ignoring presses. A field that had focus (Enter pressed in it) gets it
back when the form is done. (`@submit` is a handler prop, as in Nuxt UI, so
the form can wait for it.) The native form has `novalidate`: Weft shows the
errors, not the browser.

<script setup vapor lang="ts">
import { reactive, ref, useTemplateRef } from 'vue'
import { Button, Form, FormField, Input } from '@weft/ui'

const state = reactive({ username: '' })
const form = useTemplateRef<{ setErrors(errors: Record<string, string>): void }>('form')
const busy = ref(false)

// A stand-in for the server's answer: the name is taken.
async function save(values: { username: string }) {
  busy.value = true
  await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 600))
  busy.value = false
  form.value?.setErrors({ username: `"${values.username}" is taken; try another.` })
}
</script>

<template>
  <Form ref="form" :state="state" :schema="{ username: { required: true, min: 3 } }" @submit="save">
    <FormField label="Username" name="username"><Input v-model="state.username" /></FormField>
    <Button type="submit" label="Claim it" :loading="busy" />
  </Form>
</template>

components.name: FormField
components.purpose: The label, description, hint, error and required marker around one form control.
components.use: Around every form control that needs a visible label, inside a Form or not.
components.avoid: For a Checkbox or Switch whose own label says everything, the control alone is enough.

adapts.input: Nothing of its own; the control inside it adapts.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; it fills the width of its container.

props.name: label
props.description: What the control is for. The label slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: Help in a sentence, under the label ("We never share it."). The description slot replaces it.

props.name: hint
props.description: A short note beside the label ("Optional", "3 of 10"). The hint slot replaces it.

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong, under the control; `true` marks it invalid without a sentence. Wins over the Form's error.

props.name: required
props.description: Marks the field required (an asterisk, and aria-required on the control); a Form's schema can say so too.

props.name: name
props.description: The field's name: the control's name, and the key of its value, rules and error in a Form.

props.name: id
props.description: The control's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`, for the label and the control.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables the control.

components.notes:
The label sits over the control and is `for` it: the control takes the
field's id (set `id` to choose it). A control that is not a labelable element
- a RadioGroup, a CheckboxGroup, a Slider - is named through
`aria-labelledby` instead, and the label then has no `for` (on the server
the label keeps it until the island hydrates, as the control's setup runs
after the label is written). A range Slider names each thumb by the label and
its own end: "Price Minimum".

`description` is a sentence under the label; `hint` is a short note beside
it ("Optional", "3 of 10"); `error` sits under the control. All three
describe the control through `aria-describedby`, in that order, and an
error marks it `aria-invalid`. `error: true` marks it invalid without a
sentence (or with the `error` slot). `required` draws an asterisk, hidden
from assistive technology, and sets `aria-required` on the control. The
default slot receives `{ error }`, for a control drawn by hand.

**In a Form,** `name` links the field to the Form: it shows the Form's error
for that name, it is required when the schema says so, and leaving or
changing the control lets the Form check it again. An `error` given to the
field wins over the Form's.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: A Lucide icon by name, drawn as an inline SVG in the current text colour.
components.use: Wherever an icon helps recognition, beside a label or, with a label of its own, standing alone; Weft components take the same names in their icon prop.
components.avoid: For pictures and logos, use an img; never let an icon alone carry meaning without a label.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; an icon is not a hit target, so put it in a Button or Link for one.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the surrounding text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: name
props.description: The Lucide icon's name, as on lucide.dev: `trash`, `chevron-down`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the icon is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label
props.description: What the icon means, for an icon that stands alone; without it the icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

components.notes:
Names are Lucide's, as listed on lucide.dev/icons: `trash`, `chevron-down`.
Only the icons a build uses ship: the build finds static names in templates
(`name="trash"`, `icon="plus"`) and `icon: '…'` properties in scripts, and
fails with a sentence naming the file for a name Lucide does not have. Names
made at run time go in the `icons` option of `weftIcons()`.

Without `label` the icon is decorative (`aria-hidden="true"`); with one it is
an image with that accessible name (`role="img"`). `size` is `sm` (16 px),
`md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it the icon is 1.25em.

components.name: Input
components.purpose: A one-line text field in a box that can hold an icon, a unit or a button before and after the text.
components.use: For a short answer typed in full - a name, an email address, a search - bound with v-model, usually inside a FormField.
components.avoid: For text over several lines, use Textarea; for a number stepped up and down, use InputNumber; for a choice from a known list, use a select or RadioGroup.

adapts.input: An md input is max(--weft-control-md, --weft-hit-min) tall, so 44 px on touch, the same height as an md Button beside it; sm and lg keep their sizes, and a pseudo-element behind the field grows the hit area to 44 px.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container; put it in a Grid or a FieldGroup to share a row.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The text, bound with `v-model`; a number with `v-model.number` or `type="number"`.

props.name: type
props.description: The native input type: `text`, `email`, `password`, `search`, `tel`, `url`, `number`.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch, as Button is.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used, so its label points here.

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the text. The leading slot replaces it.

props.name: trailingIcon
props.description: A Lucide icon after the text. The trailing slot replaces it.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress (a lookup as it is typed): a spinner after the text, and `aria-busy`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not editable.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`, for a form the browser checks.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The text changed (on each key, or on change with `.lazy`).

emits.name: blur
emits.description: The input lost focus.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The input took focus.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The native change: the text was committed.

components.notes:
Bind the text with `v-model`; `v-model.trim`, `.number` and `.lazy` work as
on a native input (`type="number"` also gives a number, or `null` when it is
empty). Attributes such as `placeholder`, `autocomplete`, `inputmode` and
`aria-label` go to the `<input>`; `class` and `style` go to the box.

**Leading and trailing.** `icon` and `trailing-icon` draw Lucide icons, hidden
from assistive technology; the `leading` and `trailing` slots replace them
with anything (a unit, a clear button). A press on the box outside the text
focuses the text; a button in the box keeps its own press.

**Loading** puts a spinner after the text and sets `aria-busy`; the field
stays editable (a lookup runs as it is typed).

**In a FormField** the input takes the field's id (so the label points to
it), its name, `aria-describedby` (the description, the hint and the error; an
`aria-describedby` of its own comes first), `aria-invalid` and
`aria-required`. In a FieldGroup it takes the group's size.

**For other components:** a template ref's `focus()` focuses the text, and
`input` is the element; Select, Combobox and DatePicker build on this box.

components.name: InputNumber
components.purpose: A number typed or stepped up and down, kept between a minimum and a maximum.
components.use: For a quantity, a count or an amount where a step up or down is natural.
components.avoid: For a value picked along a range, use Slider; for numbers that are really codes (a phone number, a card), use Input.

adapts.input: md is 44 px tall on touch, as an md Button is, and the steppers become large buttons, 44 px wide (28 px on pointer) and at least 44 px tall through their hit areas.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The number, bound with `v-model`; null when it is empty.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The number to start with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: min
props.description: The smallest it may be.

props.name: max
props.description: The largest it may be.

props.name: step
props.description: How much a step (an arrow key or a stepper) changes it.

props.name: wheel
props.description: Change it with the mouse wheel while it has focus. Off by default, so scrolling the page never changes a value.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`; a FieldGroup's size applies when not set. md is 44 px tall on touch, as Button is.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

props.name: decrementLabel
props.description: The decrease button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: incrementLabel
props.description: The increase button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled, steppers too.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not changeable.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The number changed: stepped, or typed and committed.

emits.name: blur
emits.description: The input lost focus.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The input took focus.

components.notes:
Bind the number with `v-model`; it is `null` when the field is empty.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern): Up and Down step by `step`,
Page Up and Page Down by ten steps, Home and End go to `min` and `max`.
Typed text is read when it is committed - Enter, or leaving the field - and
kept within `min` and `max`; text that is not a number goes back to the
value. Stepping by decimals leaves no floating-point dust (0.1 + 0.2 is 0.3).

**Mouse wheel:** off by default, so scrolling the page never changes a value.
With `wheel`, the wheel steps it, but only while it has focus.

**Steppers:** out of the tab order (the keys do their work), named by
`decrement-label` and `increment-label` ("Decrease", "Increase"), disabled at
the bounds, and a press keeps focus where it was. The input is a text input
with `role="spinbutton"` and `inputmode="decimal"`, carrying
`aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`.

components.name: Island
components.purpose: Renders a component on the server and makes it interactive in the browser, on load, when idle, when visible or when a media query matches.
components.use: For the few interactive parts of an otherwise static page, a counter, a form, a menu, so only they ship JavaScript.
components.avoid: For content that never changes in the browser, render the component directly; a page with no island ships no script at all.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; the island's component adapts as it would anywhere.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: when
props.description: When the browser hydrates it: at `load`, when `idle`, when `visible`, or when `media` matches.

props.name: media
props.description: The media query for `when="media"`, such as `(min-width: 1024px)`.

props.name: component
props.description: The `<script setup>` SFC to render and hydrate; its file name is the island's id.

props.name: props
props.description: Props for the component, sent to the browser as JSON.

components.notes:
The component must be a `<script setup>` single-file component: its file name
is the island's id. `props` travel to the browser as JSON, so they may hold
only strings, finite numbers, booleans, null, arrays and plain objects; the
build refuses anything else with a sentence naming the prop. `when="media"`
needs a `media` query. Ids from `useId` inside an island are counted per
island, so they match between the server and the browser.

Ids are counted by the island's position among the page's islands, the
same on the server (render order) and in the browser (document order). So an
island inside a `<Teleport>`, whose markup lands elsewhere in the document,
is not supported: its position, and so its ids, would differ.

The page inlines the CSS of everything the island's component imports, not
only what it draws on the server, since the browser may draw the rest later
(a menu that opens, a field that appears). So an island that imports the
`@weft/ui` index, `import { Button } from '@weft/ui'`, carries the stylesheet
of every Weft component. Import components by path in an island instead:
`import Button from '@weft/ui/basics/Button.vue'` (the path is the
component's file under `src/`). Outside islands it makes no difference: the
page carries only the CSS of the components it renders.

It has no stylesheet of its own: `<weft-island>` is an unstyled element around the component.

components.name: Kbd
components.purpose: A key on the keyboard, for showing shortcuts.
components.use: In help text, menus and tooltips, one Kbd per key of a shortcut.
components.avoid: For code or a value to copy, use a code element.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; show shortcuts only where a keyboard is likely, which the page decides.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: value
props.description: The key: a character (`K`) or a name with a symbol (`command`, `shift`, `option`, `enter`, `backspace`, `tab`, `arrowup`…). The default slot replaces it.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

components.notes:
`value` is a character (`K`) or a key name. Names with a symbol draw the
symbol and say the name to assistive technology, which reads symbols poorly:
`command` (⌘), `shift` (⇧), `option` (⌥), `enter` (↵), `backspace` (⌫),
`tab` (⇥) and the arrows `arrowup`, `arrowdown`, `arrowleft`, `arrowright`.
Any other value is drawn as given. It draws what it is told and never guesses
the reader's operating system, so the server and browser agree. The default
slot replaces the value.

components.name: Link
components.purpose: A link to another page or site, marking itself when it is the current page.
components.use: For navigation, in running text, in a list of pages or a footer.
components.avoid: For an action that changes something, use Button; for a link that should look like a button, use Button with to.

adapts.input: A standalone link (in a list, a footer, a toolbar) gets a hit area of at least 44 px on touch through a pseudo-element; a link in running text keeps its text size and no larger hit area, which would cover the lines around it. Hover styles apply only where the device can hover.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: to
props.description: The address.

props.name: href
props.description: The address, for those who write links as HTML does; `to` wins.

props.name: external
props.description: Another site: adds rel="noopener". Unset, an address with a scheme and host (`https://…`, `//…`) is external.

props.name: target
props.description: Where to open it, as the native attribute: `_blank` for a new tab.

props.name: rel
props.description: The native rel; `noopener` is added for an external link.

props.name: active
props.description: This link is the current page: sets aria-current="page". Unset, the link compares its address with the browser's.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: no address, so not focusable, and announced as a disabled link.

props.name: standalone
props.description: Not in running text (a list of links, a footer, a toolbar): drawn as an inline box whose hit area is at least --weft-hit-min on touch. In a sentence, leave it unset, so the hit area does not cover the lines around it.

emits.name: click
emits.description: Followed by mouse, touch or keyboard; never while disabled.

components.notes:
**Standalone or in text.** Set `standalone` on a link that stands on its
own: in navigation, a list, a footer, a toolbar. It becomes an inline box
whose hit area reaches `--weft-hit-min` (44 px on touch). Leave it unset in
running text: a larger hit area there would cover the line above and below
and take taps meant for the links on them (WCAG 2.5.8 exempts targets in a
sentence).

The text is the theme's `--weft-color-primary-text`, which it checks for
4.5:1 on the page.

An external link (an address with a scheme and host, `https://…` or `//…`,
or any with `external`) gets `rel="noopener"`, added to any `rel` you give.
`target` passes through as the native attribute.

The link to the page the browser is on gets `aria-current="page"`. It is
worked out in the browser after mounting, so the server's markup and the
first client render agree; on a page with no JavaScript the server cannot
know, so set `active` where the layout knows the current page. `active`
always wins over the comparison.

**Disabled:** no address and no target, so it leaves the tab order;
announced as a disabled link (`role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`); a click
does nothing.

**Keyboard:** a native anchor, so Tab reaches it and Enter follows it.

**In a Form** that is disabled or busy (submitting), a Link is disabled, so
it cannot navigate mid-submit: a disabled fieldset leaves links alone, so the
Link reads the Form itself.

components.name: Page
components.purpose: The main landmark of a page, with its title, description, actions and content.
components.use: Once per page, as the outermost layout component, so the page has one main, one h1 and the surface's width and spacing.
components.avoid: For a titled part inside a page, use Section; for a box of related content, use Card.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.

adapts.width: Nothing changes in the component itself; the header's actions wrap under the title when they do not fit beside it.

props.name: title
props.description: The page's heading, rendered as its h1.

props.name: description
props.description: A line under the title saying what the page is for.

components.notes:

title and description with your own markup, and the `actions` slot for
buttons beside them.

components.name: PinInput
components.purpose: A short code typed one character per box.
components.use: For a one-time code, a verification code or a PIN.
components.avoid: For a password or anything longer than about eight characters, use Input.

adapts.input: Every box is its own target, so md and sm boxes are 44 px square on touch (36 and 28 px on pointer); with type number a number pad comes up.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: The boxes stay in one row.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The code, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The code to start with when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: length
props.description: How many boxes.

props.name: type
props.description: `number` takes digits only and brings up a number pad; `text` takes letters and digits.

props.name: mask
props.description: Hide what is typed, as a password field does.

props.name: otp
props.description: A one-time code: lets the browser fill it from a message (autocomplete="one-time-code").

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown in each empty box.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: the joined code posts under it.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: every box natively disabled.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`, on each box.

props.name: boxLabel
props.description: A box's name for assistive technology; `{n}` is its number and `{count}` how many there are.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A box changed: the joined code.

emits.name: complete
emits.description: Every box is filled: the code.

components.notes:
Bind the joined code with `v-model`; `complete` fires once every box is
filled. `length` sets how many boxes (5). `type="number"` takes digits only;
`mask` hides what is typed; `otp` lets the browser fill a one-time code from
a message (`autocomplete="one-time-code"`).

**Keyboard:** typing a character fills the box and moves to the next;
Backspace clears the box, or steps back and clears the one before when it is
empty; Delete clears the box; Left and Right move (swapped in a right-to-left
document); Home and End go to the first and last box. A paste or an autofill
fills the boxes from the one it lands in, dropping characters the type does
not take.

The boxes form a `role="group"`, named by its FormField's label; each box is
named by its place (`box-label`, "Character 1 of 6"). With `name` the code
posts from a hidden input.

components.name: Popover
components.purpose: Content that floats beside a trigger, opened by a press: filters, a short form, details.
components.use: For a small panel of controls or information tied to one button, which the user opens, uses and closes.
components.avoid: For a list of actions, use DropdownMenu; for a short hint on hover, Tooltip; for a task that needs the user's full attention, Dialog.

adapts.input: On pointer it floats beside the trigger and is not modal. On touch the same content is a bottom sheet over a backdrop, modal, with `title` as its heading. The input can change while it is open; what is inside keeps its state and focus.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Floating, it stays within the room left on its side, flipping and sliding to stay in view; as a sheet it is the viewport's width.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where it floats against the trigger on pointer: `bottom`, `top-start`, … (start and end follow the text direction).

props.name: offset
props.description: The gap to the trigger, in px.

props.name: title
props.description: Names the content for assistive technology; on touch it is the sheet's heading too.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press outside close it.

props.name: modal
props.description: Modal on pointer too: focus is trapped and the page does not scroll. On touch it is always modal.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Move focus into the content when it opens (on pointer); false keeps focus where it is, as a combobox's input needs.

props.name: anchor
props.type: { getBoundingClientRect(): DOMRect /** For a point: the element it belongs to, whose scrolling and direction the overlay follows. */ contextElement?: Element }
props.description: Float against this element or point instead of the trigger.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, a press outside or focus leaving.

components.notes:
The default slot is the trigger, one element (a Button); a press on it
toggles the popover, and it carries `aria-haspopup="dialog"`,
`aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`. The `content` slot is what it shows,
and gets `close()`. Bind `v-model:open` to open it from code; `anchor`
positions it against another element or a point.

The content renders into `#weft-overlays` at the end of the body (created
when first needed), only once mounted, so the server renders none of it. It
is a `role="dialog"` named by `title` (or an `aria-label`); attributes go to
it.

**Focus.** On open, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside, or to
the content itself (`auto-focus="false"` keeps it where it is, as a combobox
does). On pointer it is not modal: Tab can leave, and focus leaving closes it
(unless it went to an overlay opened from inside). With `modal`, or on touch,
focus is trapped and the page does not scroll.

**Closing.** Escape and a press outside close it (`dismissible="false"`
turns both off); a press on its trigger toggles it shut. Focus returns to
the trigger, except after a press outside, which put the user's attention
elsewhere. On touch a press on the backdrop closes it and does return focus.

`placement` is a floating-ui placement (`bottom`, `top-start`, …); `start`
and `end` follow the text direction.

components.name: Progress
components.purpose: A bar showing how far a task has got, or that it is under way when that is unknown.
components.use: For uploads, imports, multi-step work and quotas, where the reader waits or watches.
components.avoid: For a short wait inside a control, use Spinner; for loading content, use Skeleton.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; the bar fills the width it is given.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: How far along, from 0 to `max`; `null` or unset for unknown (indeterminate).

props.name: max
props.description: The value at completion.

props.name: label
props.description: What it measures, for assistive technology ("Uploading report.pdf").

props.name: tone
props.description: The bar's colour and what it says.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the bar's thickness.

props.name: status
props.description: Show the percentage beside the bar (determinate only).

components.notes:
Bind the value with `v-model` (or `model-value`), from 0 to `max` (100);
values outside are clamped. `null` or no value is indeterminate: a bar that
sweeps, which stands still at full length, dimmed, under reduced motion.
`status` shows the percentage beside the bar.

It is a `progressbar` with `aria-valuemin`, `aria-valuemax` and, when
determinate, `aria-valuenow`. Name it with `label` ("Uploading report.pdf")
or an `aria-labelledby`. The bar fills along the inline direction, so from
the right in a right-to-left document.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.purpose: One choice among a few options, all in view.
components.use: For a choice of two to six options the reader should compare at a glance (a plan, a shipping speed).
components.avoid: For many options, use a select; for on or off, use Switch or Checkbox.

adapts.input: Each row is at least 44 px tall on touch, and each radio's hit area 44 px square.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Horizontal groups wrap onto more rows when narrow.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The chosen value, bound with `v-model`; undefined or null when none is.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value chosen at first when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: items
props.description: The options: values, or `{ value, label, description, disabled }`.

props.name: legend
props.description: The group's name, shown above it; inside a FormField the field's label names it instead.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name the radios share; a FormField's applies, else one is generated.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the chosen radio.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `vertical` (a column) or `horizontal` (a wrapping row). The arrow keys work the same either way.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Disables every radio.

props.name: required
props.description: A choice must be made: the native `required` on the radios.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A radio was chosen, by press, Space or an arrow key.

components.notes:
Bind the chosen value with `v-model`; give the options as `items` - values,
or `{ value, label, description, disabled }`.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA radio group pattern): the group is one tab stop,
on the chosen radio or else the first. Down and Right move to the next radio
and choose it, Up and Left to the previous, wrapping at the ends and
skipping disabled radios; in a right-to-left document Left and Right swap.
Focus arriving by Tab or a click chooses nothing by itself; Space chooses
the focused radio.

The radios are native, sharing `name` (one is generated when not given), so
they post with a plain form. The group is `role="radiogroup"`, named by
`legend` or by its FormField's label, described by the field's description, hint and
error, and `aria-required` when the field (or `required`) asks.

components.avoid: For a plain rule, use Divider; for space alone, use the gap of a Stack or Grid; for a new titled part, use Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.

props.name: decorative

from assistive technology (`role="none"`, `aria-hidden="true"`), for a rule
that separates nothing a reader needs told about. `orientation="vertical"` stretches to the height
of its row.

components.name: Sheet
components.purpose: A modal panel that slides in from an edge of the viewport: a slideover from the side, or a bottom sheet.
components.use: For navigation on small screens, filters, a detail view or a form that should keep the page visible beside it.
components.avoid: For a short decision, use Dialog or ConfirmDialog; for content tied to one button on a large screen, Popover.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; on touch its close button's hit area is at least 44 px. Popover and DropdownMenu render as a bottom sheet on touch with this stylesheet.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: A side sheet is at most 24rem wide, the full width when the viewport is narrower; a top or bottom sheet is the viewport's width and at most 85% of its height.

props.name: open
props.description: Open or closed, bound with `v-model:open`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open when `v-model:open` is not bound.

props.name: title
props.description: The heading, which names the sheet. Without one, give the sheet an `aria-label`.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the title, which describes the sheet.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button (×) in the header.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Escape and a press on the backdrop close it.

props.name: side
props.description: The side it comes from: `start` and `end` (the inline sides, mirrored right to left), `top` or `bottom`.

emits.name: update:open
emits.description: Opened or closed, by the trigger, Escape, the backdrop or a close.

components.notes:
`side` is `start` or `end` (the inline sides, so mirrored in a right-to-left
document), `top` or `bottom`; the default is `end`. Otherwise it is used as
Dialog is: the default slot is the trigger, or bind `v-model:open`; `title`
and `description` name and describe it; `header`, `actions`, `body` and
`footer` slots, the last two with `close()`.

It is a modal dialog (WAI-ARIA APG, Dialog (Modal)): focus is trapped inside,
the page does not scroll, and Escape, the backdrop and the close button
close it (`dismissible="false"` keeps Escape and the backdrop from it), with
focus back on the trigger. The body scrolls when long.

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: A placeholder in the shape of content that is still loading.
components.use: Where text, an avatar or a card will appear, so the layout does not jump when it arrives.
components.avoid: For a wait with no shape to show, use Spinner; when the progress is known, use Progress.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; its default height is one line of the surface's text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; without a width it fills its container.

props.name: width
props.description: Any CSS length; without it, the full width.

props.name: height
props.description: Any CSS length; without it, one line of text (1em).

props.name: circle

components.notes:

and one line (1em) high. `circle` makes it round, for an avatar.

It pulses, and stands still under `prefers-reduced-motion`. It is hidden
from assistive technology: set `aria-busy="true"` on the region that is
loading, and remove it when the content arrives.

components.name: Slider
components.purpose: A value, or a range between two values, picked along a track.
components.use: For a value where the position matters more than the exact number (volume, a price range).
components.avoid: For an exact number, use InputNumber; for a few named steps, use RadioGroup.

adapts.input: The thumb is drawn 16 px (12 sm, 20 lg) on pointer and 24 px on touch (--weft-thumb-min), where a finger covers it; on touch its hit area and the track's grow to 44 px through pseudo-elements, and the slider is 44 px tall.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container; vertical sliders are 160 px tall.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The value, or an array of values for a range, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The value to start with when `v-model` is not bound; an array for a range.

props.name: min
props.description: The start of the track.

props.name: max
props.description: The end of the track.

props.name: step
props.description: The values it moves between, counted from `min`.

props.name: minStepsBetweenThumbs
props.description: For a range: the fewest steps kept between neighbouring thumbs.

props.name: orientation
props.description: `horizontal` (min at the inline start) or `vertical` (min at the bottom).

props.name: thumbLabels
props.description: Each thumb's name for assistive technology; for a range the default is "Minimum", "Value 2 of 3"… and "Maximum". A single thumb takes the Slider's own aria-label, or its FormField's label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name: each value posts under it from a hidden input.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the track's thickness and the thumb's size.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour of the filled part and the thumbs.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: out of the tab order, and presses do nothing.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: A thumb moved, by key, press or drag.

emits.name: change
emits.description: A move ended: a key press, or a drag let go; the final value.

components.notes:
Bind a number with `v-model`, or an array for a range: a thumb is drawn per
value, thumbs never pass each other (`min-steps-between-thumbs` keeps a gap),
and the track between them fills.

**Keyboard** (the WAI-ARIA slider pattern): each thumb is a `role="slider"`
in the tab order. Right and Up raise it by `step`, Left and Down lower it,
Page Up and Page Down move ten steps, Home and End go to the ends. In a
right-to-left document Left and Right swap, and the track fills from the
right. Each thumb's `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax` are its neighbours.

**Pointer:** a press on the track moves the nearest thumb there, on a step,
and drags it until let go. `update:modelValue` fires as it moves; `change`
fires once a move ends (a key press, or a drag let go).

Thumbs are named by `thumb-labels`, or for a range "Minimum" and "Maximum"
(a thumb between them "Value 2 of 3");
a single thumb takes the Slider's own `aria-label`, or its FormField's label.
In a FormField a range's thumbs are named by the label and their own name
("Price Minimum"). With `name`
each value posts from a hidden input.

components.name: Spinner
components.purpose: A turning ring for work in progress of unknown length.
components.use: Inside something that is loading, or alone where content will appear; Button shows one itself when loading.
components.avoid: When the progress is known, use Progress; for the shape of content still loading, use Skeleton.

adapts.input: Nothing changes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; without a size it scales with the text.
adapts.width: Nothing changes.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` 16 px, `md` 20 px, `lg` 24 px; without it the spinner is 1.25em, sized with the text.

props.name: label
props.description: What is happening, announced politely ("Loading invoices"); without it the spinner is decorative.

components.notes:
It turns in the text colour. Without `label` it is decorative
(`aria-hidden`); with one it is a `status` that announces the label
politely. `size` is `sm` (16 px), `md` (20 px) or `lg` (24 px); without it
the spinner is 1.25em. Under reduced motion it turns slowly rather than
freezing, since a still ring reads as stuck.

components.name: Stack
components.purpose: Lays its children out in a column or a row with a gap from the spacing scale.
components.use: For any run of things one after another, a form's fields, a toolbar's buttons, a card's lines, instead of margins or a wrapper with its own CSS.
components.avoid: For columns that should reflow with the space available, use Grid; for a page or a titled part of one, use Page or Section.

adapts.input: Nothing changes; hit targets are the children's own.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes; the gap scale is the same spacing tokens on landing and app.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a row stays a row, so give it wrap when its children may not fit a narrow container.

props.name: direction
props.description: Lay the children out top to bottom (`column`) or along the line (`row`).

props.name: gap
props.description: Space between children, from the spacing scale (`--weft-space-*`).

props.name: align
props.description: Cross-axis alignment of the children.

props.name: justify
props.description: Main-axis distribution of the children; `between` pushes them to the ends.

props.name: wrap
props.description: Let a row wrap onto more lines when its children do not fit.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render, for semantics: `ul`, `nav`, `form`.

components.notes:
`gap` takes the spacing scale (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8, from `--weft-space-*`).
`align` and `justify` work along the cross and main axes as in flexbox, and
`as` renders another element, such as `ul` or `nav`, for the right semantics.

components.purpose: On or off, taking effect at once.
components.use: For a setting that applies as soon as it changes (Wi-Fi, notifications).
components.avoid: For a choice sent with a form (accept the terms), use Checkbox.

adapts.input: The track keeps its drawn size; its hit area is at least 44 px square on touch, and the row at least 44 px tall.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: Nothing changes; a long label wraps beside the track.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: On or off, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The state to start in when `v-model` is not bound.

props.name: label
props.description: The text beside the switch. The default slot replaces it.

props.name: description
props.description: A sentence under the label, which also describes the switch.

props.name: value
props.description: What a form post sends while it is on (default `on`).

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The input's id; generated when not set.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour while on.

props.name: loading
props.description: Work in progress (the change is being saved): a spinner in the thumb, aria-busy, and no toggling.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`: it must be on.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: Turned on or off.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The native change.

components.name: Textarea
components.purpose: Text over several lines, which can grow with what is typed.
components.use: For a message, a description, a note; with autoresize where the length varies.
components.avoid: For one line, use Input; for formatted text, use an editor.

adapts.input: It is never shorter than an md control, so at least 44 px on touch whatever its rows and size.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills the width of its container.

props.name: modelValue
props.description: The text, bound with `v-model`.

props.name: rows
props.description: Lines shown, and with autoresize the fewest it shrinks to.

props.name: autoresize
props.description: Grow with the text, from `rows` up to `maxrows`.

props.name: maxrows
props.description: With autoresize, the most lines it grows to before it scrolls; 0 for no limit.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm`, `md` or `lg`: the text size and padding.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown while it is empty; not a label.

props.name: name
props.description: The form field name; a FormField's name applies when not set.

props.name: id
props.description: The textarea's id; inside a FormField the field's id is used.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Unavailable: natively disabled.

props.name: readonly
props.description: Shown but not editable.

props.name: required
props.description: The native `required`.

emits.name: update:modelValue
emits.description: The text changed (on each key, or on change with `.lazy`).

emits.name: blur
emits.description: The textarea lost focus.

emits.name: focus
emits.description: The textarea took focus.

emits.name: change
emits.description: The native change: the text was committed.

components.notes:
Bind the text with `v-model` (`.trim` and `.lazy` work). `rows` sets how many
lines show (3). With `autoresize` it grows as text is added, from `rows` up to
`maxrows` (0, the default, for no limit) and then scrolls, and it shrinks
back when text is removed; it cannot be resized by hand then. A template ref
has `focus()`, `resize()` (to fit after being shown) and `textarea`.

In a FormField it takes the field's id, name, description, error and required
state, as Input does. Attributes go to the `<textarea>`.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: One short message that appears for a moment, with an optional action: saved, sent, undone.
components.use: Rendered by Toaster from useToast(); render one yourself only inside a live region of your own.
components.avoid: To show a toast, call useToast().add and put a Toaster in the layout; for a message that must stay, use an inline alert.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; its close button's hit area is at least 44 px on touch.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: It fills its Toaster's column.

props.name: title
props.description: The message, in bold.

props.name: description
props.description: More about it, under the title.

props.name: tone
props.description: The colour and what it says: `success`, `danger`, …

props.name: icon
props.description: A Lucide icon before the text.

props.name: duration
props.description: ms before it leaves on its own; default `--weft-duration-toast`; 0 stays until closed.

props.name: paused
props.description: Its time stands still: hovered, or focus inside.

props.name: close
props.description: Show the close button.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The close button's name for assistive technology.

props.name: actions
props.description: Buttons after the text; each closes the toast after it runs.

emits.name: close
emits.description: It should go: its time ran out, or it was closed or acted on.

components.notes:
`title`, `description`, `icon` (a Lucide name), `tone` (a bar at the inline
start), `actions` (buttons, each closing the toast after it runs) and a
close button (× drawn inline; `close="false"` hides it). The default,
`leading` and `actions` slots replace the text, icon and actions.

It emits `close` when it should go: after `duration` ms (by default the
theme's `--weft-duration-toast`, 4000 ms in the neutral theme; 0 stays until
closed), when closed, acted on, or on Escape while focus is in it. Its time
stands still while `paused`, and resumes with what it had left.

components.name: Toaster
components.purpose: Shows the toasts queued with useToast(), in a corner of the viewport, announced to assistive technology.
components.use: Once, in the app's layout; then call useToast().add from anywhere in the browser.
components.avoid: For a message tied to a form or a section, show it there instead.

adapts.input: Nothing changes in behaviour; toasts' buttons follow Button's touch sizes.
adapts.surface: Nothing changes in behaviour; text follows the surface's type scale.
adapts.width: At most 24rem wide, the viewport less a margin when narrower.

props.name: position
props.description: Where toasts stack: a corner, or the middle of the top or bottom edge.

props.name: max
props.description: How many show at once, the newest; the rest wait their turn.

props.name: label
props.description: The region's name for assistive technology.

components.notes:
const toast = useToast()
    toast.add({ title: 'Saved', description: 'Your draft is safe.', tone: 'success' })
    toast.add({ title: 'Deleted', actions: [{ label: 'Undo', onClick: restore }] })

`add` returns the toast with its `id`, for `update(id, patch)` and
`remove(id)`; `clear()` empties the queue and `toasts` reads it. A toast
leaves after its `duration`, by default the theme's `--weft-duration-toast`.

The Toaster is a region named "Notifications" (`label`) whose list is a
polite live region, so a new toast is announced without moving focus. While
the pointer is over it or focus is inside it, no toast's time runs. F8 moves
focus to it, to reach a toast's actions; when the focused toast goes, focus
stays in the region. `position` is a corner or the middle of the top or
bottom edge (`bottom-end` by default; start and end follow the text
direction), and `max` (5) toasts show at once, the newest.

It renders into the overlay root only once mounted. The queue is one per
page; on the server `add` does nothing.
